name: Anzu
sum: Large caenagnathid from the upper Maastrichtian Hell Creek Formation of the United States, known from several skeletons.
holotype: CM 78000, a mostly disarticulated partial skeleton found in 1998 by Fred Nuss on a private ranch in South Dakota, Hell Creek Formation.
material: Numerous skeletons preserving cranial and postcranial elements.
biology: Named after Anzû, a bird-like daemon of Mesopotamian religion; its first skeletons seem to have been transported by water before burial. Its body mass was estimated by Atkins-Weltman (2021).
author: Lamanna et al. 2014

sources.text: M. C. Lamanna, H.-D. Sues, and E. R. Schachner, T. R. Lyson. 2014. A New large-bodied oviraptorosaurian theropod dinosaur from the latest Cretaceous of western North America. PLoS ONE 9(3):e92022:1-16
